html:
SMTO-CMP-0039 — The AI used a failed step as proof that the task worked

GUID: 540c32ad-e504-4328-a113-88f19ec8c07a
Slug: completion-unsuccessful-evidence
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • The AI pointed to a step as proof the task was done, but that step didn't succeed, so it does not establish that the task worked. SMTO asked the AI to fix the problem or report it honestly.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Expand the task and open the step marked Failed or Stopped to read its error message. The error usually names the cause, such as a missing file, a wrong path or a missing permission.
  2. Fix that cause if it's something you control, such as restoring a file or giving access. The same step will fail again until its cause is fixed.
  3. Send a message asking SMTO to check the current state, then redo only what's missing. A failed step can still change part of something, so checking first avoids doing it twice.

What success looks like

  • A later step succeeds where the failed one didn't, and the task finishes as Completed.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking for it again. Open Technical details, select Copy error details and send them, with the step's error, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't rerun the whole task; steps that worked would run again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Completion was rejected because a cited result has neither success status nor an eligible complete read observation (for example error, failed or cancelled), so it does not establish success; the neutral-write, unexecuted and running cases are reported separately.

What this means

  • A cited result has neither success nor an eligible complete observation, after more specific neutral-write/unexecuted/running cases are excluded. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • A cited result has neither success nor an eligible complete observation, after more specific neutral-write/unexecuted/running cases are excluded.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect its actual status and concrete failure rather than treating any returned receipt as success.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the cited receipt's status and concrete error in completion_feedback.open_requirements. Resolve the failure and cite a later successful result or complete observation, or have the model report partial or failed accurately; never treat a returned receipt as success by itself.
  • Inspect the unsuccessful operation and resolve the missing outcome before declaring success.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Completion uses eligible authoritative evidence or accurately reports the unresolved outcome.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
